title: Re-audit R2: Opus 5.5 (local) A2-F1..F4 @ 9106487d
description:
Bounded re-audit of the second-audit repairs at the repaired candidate 9106487d9a094f4d39914ed135e2da7e5371af3d (main after PR #717; pack bytes = 73083baf). The charter is in .worktrees/.dispatch/eshyra-o9bd.19.6.7.reaudit-common.md (also embedded in each launch prompt). The finder re-checks its OWN findings: is each class closed for its whole class at this candidate, and did the repair introduce a new defect in the touched area? This is not a new broad audit. Report: identity checks; per finding CLOSED / NOT CLOSED / REGRESSED with evidence; new material findings in touched areas only; LIMITS; final line RE-AUDIT RESULT: CLEAN or BLOCKERS (<n>).

SCOPE: A2-F1 death-save bonuses (PR #710), A2-F2 DM time guidance and advance_time lifecycle (PR #712), A2-F3 custody plus the single writer per campaign database (PR #711, ADR 0012), A2-F4 level-up HP minimum credited to the 2018 errata by user decision (PR #713).

A2-F1 | CLOSED | Death saves now apply saving-throw bonuses on both paths.
- Reproducer p01-death-save.mts (real registry, both paths):

  - Exhaustive invariant against an SRD p.98 oracle: natural 1..20 x saveBonus -20..20 x five starting counter states, on both the character and combatant paths, 8,200 cases, 0 mismatches. The oracle: natural 1 is two failures, natural 20 revives, otherwise success when natural + bonus is at least 10. Third successes stabilize; on the combatant path the seeded schedule is created.

Residual, BLOCKER: the repaired dawn guidance presumes a time of day the DM cannot see.
- Invariant and authority:
  - Dawn-keyed item economies regain at the game world's dawn. Example: Wand of Secrets, SRD p.249, "regains 1d3 expended charges daily at dawn". 63 pack magic-item records carry a dawn reset, Robe of Stars a dusk reset, and Bag of Tricks and Oathbow a next-dawn ending.
  - The repair bead's own acceptance (eshyra-o9bd.19.6.7.7): the protocol "routes dawn/rest recharge consistently with the real tool contracts (pack-bound item economies included)", and "pack-bound items recharge at dawn ... through that DM-directed path".
  - ADR 0020 §3, and §5.9 conditions 4, 6 and 9 (truthful in-band scope; a capability in force declares its inputs and exclusions; explicit limits).
  - Precedent: A2-F2 itself was dispositioned as a blocker, as was o9bd.16 L3-F2/F3 (in-band guidance contradicting the live contract).
- Evidence at 9106487d:
  - protocol.ts:308-310 (new in #712): "At dawn, use `advance_time` to pass time and recharge canonical pack-bound item economies; use `reset_usage` only for generic/legacy unbound dawn counters".
  - toolRest.ts:63 says advance_time "processes due item timers and dawn economies, including pack-bound items". It does not say when dawn is.
  - The engine's dawn is a fixed phase of the elapsed clock, defined in worldClockBoundaries.ts:9-14: elapsed counts from campaign start, a day is 1,440 minutes, dawn is minute 360 and dusk minute 1,080. The item reset executor (crossedBoundaryEvents, itemResetExecutor.ts:813-835) and the start_effect next-dawn fill (toolStartEffect.ts:79, :663) both use it.
  - The convention is written only in developer docs: docs/item-reset-executor.md:11 ("Elapsed minute zero is midnight") and :21 ("narrative labels are deliberately advisory"). eshyra-pukl decided "Convention (document it)".
  - Nothing model-facing states it. I grepped orchestrator/ and the inventory, and the advance_time entry (:1401) does not name it.
  - The clock starts at elapsed 0 with an empty label (schema.snapshot.sql:402).
  - The DM context shows only "Clock: <label> [elapsed N minutes]" (contextAssembler.ts:1054).
  - update_clock invites free time-of-day labels, e.g. "Day 3, late afternoon" (toolUpdateClock.ts:17).
- Reproducer p23-dawn-phase.mts (real registry, bundled pack, Wand of Secrets held):
  - The label is "Day 1, 8:00 AM" at elapsed 0, and all three charges are spent.
  - advance_time 600 to "Day 1, 6:00 PM" applies the dawn reset at elapsed 360 (+2 charges), at a narrated 2 PM.
  - The charges are spent again at "Day 1, 10:00 PM".
  - complete_long_rest 480 to "Day 2, 6:00 AM (dawn)" (elapsed 1,320) gives no reset and 0 charges.
  - Following the protocol's "At dawn, use advance_time" (1 minute) gives no reset.
  - The next engine dawn is elapsed 1,800, a narrated 2 PM on Day 2.
  - Under the repaired protocol, generic dawn counters reset through reset_usage at the narrated dawn, while pack-bound economies reset at the engine dawn. One campaign has two different dawns.
- Reachability: live in every campaign whose narrated time of day at elapsed 0 is not midnight. Nothing anchors it and the label starts empty. It affects every pack-bound dawn economy, the dusk economy and both next-dawn grant endings.
- Consequence:
  - Canonical charges are unavailable at the narrated dawn and come back at an unrelated narrated hour (a phase error of up to 24 h).
  - Next-dawn creatures vanish at the wrong narrated time.
  - The DM has no truthful repair: reset_usage and restore_usage do not touch pack-bound rows, and the engine's dawn is never shown.
- Siblings:
  - Phase-independent and correct: elapsed-relative lifetimes (effect expiry, stable recovery, hour/day anchored cooldowns, item timers) and round timers.
  - Affected: exactly the absolute daily boundaries, meaning dawn and dusk resets and next-dawn endings.
- Proportionate closure, either:
  - state the canonical day in band and show it: the protocol, the advance_time description and the inventory say that elapsed minute 0 is 00:00 of day 1, with dawn at 06:00 and dusk at 18:00 of each 1,440-minute day, and that narrated time of day and clock labels follow it; and the context clock line renders the derived day and time (optionally the next dawn); or
  - record a campaign start time-of-day offset once, and apply it in the executor, the next-dawn grants and the context.
- Evidence (generalized invariant): one contract test that, for any elapsed value, the rendered time of day agrees with the executor's dawn and dusk boundaries, plus one prompt test that the convention is stated.

  - Session 2 reaches L5: checkpoint K2, release rev 3.

  - Restoring K1 (sheet L2, synced 1) classifies as stale-copy (head 3, local 1). acquire is refused, release returns undefined, and the head stays rev 3 at L5.

  - The crashed original resumes as already-held, and its release commits the unsynced L6 as rev 4 (the user adjustment preserved).
  - The restored K2 copy, synced 2 with sheet equal to head 3, is already-held. Once the original syncs, it becomes stale-copy and its release is a no-op.
  - With idle custody, a K1 copy classifies as stale-copy.
- Original siblings re-checked:

  - catch-up refuses held-elsewhere.
  - Dispute replay snapshots include character_registry_sync, and gracefulClose defers release while a dispute is pending.

  - Cross-process and killed-holder lock tests pass.
  - Registry custody units are BEGIN IMMEDIATE with a head-checked append. The stamp is written after commit, and the sheet==head restamp recovers a crash in between.
  - No production caller nests a stamp-producing operation in atomically.
  - Close-and-recap re-acquires custody before the new session (playSession.ts:144-150).

NO-REQUIREMENT OBSERVATIONS (one line each):
- Level-up Constitution change under the errata minimum: the engine adds +1 per level attained, which is exactly SRD p.56 (rule:beyond-1st-level: "When your Constitution modifier increases by 1, your hit point maximum increases by 1 for each level you have attained"). SRD p.81's "as though you had the new modifier from 1st level" would credit 1 less for each level the minimum raised (p31: CON 9 Fighter rolling a natural 1 at L2, CON to 11 at L4: engine 24, p.81 reading 23). Two SRD statements diverge only under the adopted errata, and the engine follows the explicit one; Sol .9.3 saw the same. This is no defect; the user may settle it if wanted.
- Legacy residual wording: the first acquire stamps an already-stale unstamped copy at head, and its release then commits the older sheet (p16b: L1 over L7). This is "keeps the previous behaviour" as disclosed. "Not detected until it is stamped" could be read as detection afterwards, so the wording could be tightened.
- The stale-copy error from checkCustodyResumable says "advanced in another campaign" even for a restored copy of the same campaign. Wording only; the CLI UX has its own text.
- The repaired protocol no longer mentions how to apply a monster's rest. reset_usage with combatantId still supports it, and the "only for generic/legacy unbound dawn counters" clause sits inside the dawn sentence.
- The protocol's death-save line does not mention saveBonus; the tool description does.
- The rest results omit combatantStableRecoveries from the payload. The state is settled by advanceWorldTime.

PRE-EXISTING DEFECT OUTSIDE THIS RE-AUDIT'S SCOPE (reported for disposition; NOT counted in the result line, because it is neither in my findings' classes nor introduced by a repair). Monster X/Day and innate per-day economies regain at dawn and never on a long rest, contradicting SRD p.259.
- Invariant and authority: SRD 5.1 p.259 rule:limited-usage: "X/Day ... a monster must finish a long rest to regain expended uses". spend_usage and reset_usage are capabilities in force (§5.9 condition 6). The standing SRD-fidelity hard rule applies.
- Evidence:
  - usageCounters.ts:9 comments "X/Day means X uses, regained at dawn (limited-usage)", which misreads the cited rule.
  - Derived combatant economies take resetKind 'dawn': usage.perDay at :381, innate per-day groups at :506 and :515.
  - EVENT_RESETS.long_rest (:241) excludes 'dawn'.
  - The spend refusal reads "spent until dawn (reset_usage)" (:669).
  - The reset_usage description says "dawn restores per-day economies (X/Day, innate per-day spells, ...)".
  - The F5 design (eshyra-2n1t.7) recorded "perDay->dawn reset" with no SRD basis.
  - The repaired protocol (protocol.ts:309-310) routes "generic ... dawn counters" to reset_usage at dawn.
- Reproducer p40-xday.mts: Aboleth Enslave (3/Day) is spent three times and the fourth spend is refused. reset_usage long_rest scoped to the combatant resets nothing and the next spend is still refused. reset_usage dawn restores it.
- Reachability: 39 creature records with usage.perDay, plus innate per-day groups; any monster whose uses span a rest or a dawn (recurring or persistent monsters).
- Consequence: uses return at dawn without a rest and never on a long rest.
- Siblings: Recharge X-Y and "Recharge after a Short or Long Rest" map to rests correctly. Item "daily at dawn" charges map to dawn correctly.
- Closure: map creature perDay and innate per-day groups to a kind that long_rest restores; correct the refusal text, the reset_usage description and the inventory; state the monster long-rest path. Evidence: one generalized test over the derived combatant economies (per-day economies restore on long_rest, not on dawn).
- Severity: blocker-class under the standing rule. I recommend the Captain open a bead and disposition it before acceptance (eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4). It belongs to my original lane's "usageCounters reset mapping" review, where I missed it.
